title: Microbial Control and Monitoring Strategies for Cleanroom Environments and Cellular Therapies
protocol: Secure loose hair.
Wash hands thoroughly.
Change into scrubs (long-sleeve tops and full-length pants are preferable).
Gather cleanroom shoes and put on shoe covers.
Sanitize hands using an alcohol-based hand sanitizer.
Don non-sterile gloves.
If applicable, don a beard cover for any visible facial hair.
Don a non-sterile bouffant hat.
Cover forearms with non-sterile sleeves if long-sleeve tops were not used.
Remove shoe covers and step onto the tacky mat in front of the ISO8 anteroom door with each foot.
Ensure entire foot makes contact with the tacky mat before entry.
Discard shoe covers.
Decontaminate gloves and door handle with 70% sterile isopropyl alcohol (sIPA).
Enter the ISO8 anteroom.
Gather a sterile hood, sterile face mask, sterile coveralls, sterile boot covers, and safety glasses.
Decontaminate the gloves with 70% sIPA.
Don safety glasses.
Stage materials onto a clean surface.
Don a new pair of non-sterile shoe covers over dedicated cleanroom shoes.
Step onto the tacky mat in front of the secondary anteroom.
Ensure each foot makes contact with the tacky mat.
Decontaminate the gloves with 70% sIPA.
Gather staged gowning supplies and enter the secondary ISO7 anteroom, remaining on the dirty side of the demarcation line.
Don the sterile hood and the sterile coverall, touching only the inside of the material.
Tuck the neck of the hood inside the coverall to create a complete seal.
Don the secondary sterile boot covers.
Decontaminate the gloves with 70% sIPA between each donning step.
Verify that the gowning has been donned appropriately.
Decontaminating the gloves with 70% sIPA again.
Enter the ISO7 space.
Periodically inspect the gowning material for integrity.
Exit the cleanroom immediately if compromised and re-gown.
Don sterile sleeves over the coverall, using thumb loops if present.
Don sterile gloves over existing gloves, ensuring the cuff of the glove extends over the sterile sleeve.
Decontaminate the gloves with 70% sIPA between each step.
Enter the BSC.
Inspect the gowning material for integrity periodically.
Exit the cleanroom immediately and re-gown if compromised.
Exit the BSC.
Carefully remove the top pair of gloves and sterile sleeves.
Decontaminate the inner gloves with 70% sIPA.
Enter the secondary anteroom, waiting for the door to close fully between each step.
Enter the primary anteroom, waiting for the door to close fully between each step.
Remove outer sterile boot covers.
Remove coverall.
Remove hood.
Remove face mask.
Exit the primary anteroom.
Remove non-sterile gowning in the unclassified space.
Sanitize hands using an alcohol-based hand sanitizer.
Return to street clothes.
Assemble a handheld cleaning mop or obtain a clean low-lint wipe.
If using a low-lint wipe, fold the wipe into quarters and rotate between each surface.
Saturate the mop head or low-lint wipe with an approved disinfectant.
Clean the HEPA diffuser grill of the BSC using overlapping wipes.
Clean the back wall of the BSC using overlapping wipes.
Clean both side walls of the BSC using overlapping wipes.
Clean the sash of the BSC using overlapping wipes.
Wipe the work surface of the BSC using overlapping wipes.
Wipe the sash of the BSC with 70% sIPA to remove any residual disinfectant.
Decontaminate all materials requiring transfer from a non-classified or lower-classified area to a higher-classified area.
Remove the outer bag/pouch if the materials have been terminally sterilized and are in multiple bags.
Obtain a low-lint wipe and fold it into quarters.
Saturate the wipe with 70% sIPA or an approved disinfectant.
Wipe the exterior of the material/equipment using overlapping wipes.
Ensure all areas of the item are wiped, including the insides of pull-apart package seals and nooks/indents on the equipment.
Rotate the wheels of wheeled equipment to wipe the entire wheel during the staging process.
Clean the BSC starting from back to front or top to bottom.
Wipe the HEPA diffuser grill (the top of the BSC) using overlapping wipes.
Wipe the back wall of the BSC using overlapping wipes.
Wipe both side walls of the BSC using overlapping wipes.
Wipe the sash of the BSC using overlapping wipes.
Wipe the work surface of the BSC using overlapping wipes.
Wipe the sash of the BSC again using 70% sIPA to remove any residual disinfectant.
Collect and label one tryptic soy agar with lecithinase and tween (TSALT) plate for each sampling site.
Collect and label one Sabouraud dextrose agar with lecithinase and tween (SABLT) plate for each sampling site.
Aseptically remove the lid of a TSALT plate, being careful not to touch the raised agar surface.
Touch the raised agar to the surface being sampled, ensuring full contact.
Apply firm pressure to the TSALT plate.
Leave the TSALT plate in contact with the surface for at least 5 seconds.
Do not move the TSALT plate laterally over the surface during sampling.
Avoid exerting excessive force on the TSALT plate during sampling.
Aseptically remove the sampling head by gripping only the outside edge.
Place the medium into the plate holder on the sampler against the longer prong first, then secure the plate in place.
Loosely bag the plates after sampling.
Incubate the cultures as described.
Aseptically remove the plate lid.
Place the lid on a cleaned surface out of the way until sampling is completed.
Aseptically replace and secure the sampling head, gripping only the outside edge to avoid contamination.
Repeat steps for remaining medium if using a multi-headed air sampler.
Place the air sampler in the designated location with sampling heads facing the predominant airflow direction.
Ensure that exhaust from non-viable air samplers does not interfere with viable sampler.
Set the air sampler to validated settings and start the sampling cycle.
Aseptically remove the sampling head after completion, gripping only the outside edge.
Hold the sampling head in one hand and aseptically replace the lid of the agar plate.
Remove the plate from the holder.
Loosely bag the plates.
Incubate cultures as described.
Disinfect the sampling head and surrounding area with 70% sIPA.
Aseptically secure the sampling head, gripping only the outside edge.
Perform a zero check on the laser particle counter prior to sampling activities for each day of use.
Attach the isokinetic head to the sampling port of the particle counter directly or affixed to a short length of tubing if needed for the sampling location.
Set the particle counter to validated settings and delay approximately 30 seconds before starting the sampling cycle to avoid airflow disruption.
Position the laser particle counter's isokinetic head in the sampling location facing into the predominant direction of airflow movement.
Ensure the exhaust from the viable air sampler does not interfere with the non-viable sampler if both are used simultaneously.
For areas where the airflow is not unidirectional or unknown, position the isokinetic head vertically upward.
Start the sampling cycle.
Slowly exit the sampling area to avoid disrupting the airflow.
Do not aerosolize liquids near the air sampler during a sampling cycle.
Retrieve the laser particle counter when sampling is completed.
Record the average particle counts for 0.5 µm.
Repeat steps 2.3.3-2.3.6 for the next sampling location.
Wipe the outside of the non-viable particle sampler with 70% sIPA or an approved disinfectant if moving between rooms or BSCs.
Avoid getting disinfectant inside the isokinetic head.
Incubate environmental samples at 30 °C-35 °C in air for at least 3 days.
Incubate environmental samples at 20 °C-25 °C in air for at least 7 days.
Incubate TSA (settling plate) at 30 °C-35 °C in air for at least 3 days.
Incubate SAB (settling plate) at 20 °C-25 °C in air for at least 7 days.
Incubate samples at 30 °C-35 °C in air for at least 48 hours.
Continue incubation at 20 °C-25 °C for at least 5 days.
Incubate product in TSB at 20 °C-25 °C for at least 14 days.
Monitor periodically on days 3, 5, 7, and 14.
Incubate product in FTM at 30 °C-35 °C for at least 14 days.
Monitor periodically on days 3, 5, 7, and 14.
Incubate product at 30 °C-35 °C, air, for at least 14 days.
Monitor incubation using the BacT/ALERT Dual-T instrument.
Conduct a visual check of each bottle at the end of incubation for mold balls.
Test product sterility using iFN+ method at 30 °C-35 °C for at least 14 days.
Monitor automatically by the BacT/ALERT Dual-T instrument throughout incubation.
Conduct visual checks of each bottle at the end of incubation for mold balls.
Test product sterility using SAB method at 20 °C-25 °C for at least 14 days.
Monitor periodically throughout the incubation period on days 3, 5, 7, and 14.
Place labeled TSA and SAB plates near the work area.
Document the sampling start time.
Aseptically open both plates, placing the lids on a clean surface in the BSC away from the work area.
Close the lids of the plates after 4 hours maximum duration.
Loosely bag the plates.
Incubate the cultures as described in Table 1.
Obtain two labeled TSALT plates.
Aseptically remove the lid of one plate, and place it on a clean work surface away from the sampling area.
Gently roll the pad of each finger and thumb of one hand on the surface of the plate.
Sample the largest surface area of each finger/thumb rather than the tip using sufficient force to make slight depressions on the agar without cracking the surface.
Aseptically place the lid back onto the plate, and repeat for the other hand.
Sanitize the hands with 70% sIPA at the completion of sampling.
Loosely bag the plates.
Incubate the cultures as described in Table 1.
Obtain the test article and the associated TSB and FTM bottles.
Remove protective caps from septum-capped bottles and wipe the septum with a sterile alcohol wipe.
Loosen the cap of screw-top capped bottles but do not remove it completely.
Vortex the test article to ensure a homogenous suspension.
Inoculate the bottles with the validated volume of the test article using a sterile syringe and hypodermic needle for septum caps, or pipettor for screw caps.
Wipe the septum with a sterile alcohol wipe after inoculation.
Insert a sterile venting unit into septum-capped bottles to allow air exchange during incubation.
Leave the cap 1/4 to 1/2 a turn loose on screw-top bottles to allow air exchange.
Aseptically close the TSA and SAB settling plates.
Document the sampling end time.
Perform GFS as per step 3.2, wiping gloves with 70% sIPA after sampling.
Loosely bag the plates.
Incubate cultures as described in Table 1.
Transfer all test materials out of the BSC.
Clean the BSC as per step 1.4.
Obtain one labeled iFA+, one labeled iFN+, and one SAB plate for each test article.
Obtain one TSALT and one SABLT for viable surface sampling.
Obtain one TSA and one SAB plate for settling plates.
Gown for work inside the BSC as per step 1.2.
Clean the BSC as per step 1.4.
Stage the materials into the BSC as per step 1.5.
Perform contact sampling of the critical work area as per step 2.1.
Wipe the surface with 70% sIPA after sampling.
Prepare the TSA and SAB settling plates near the work area as per step 3.1.
Remove the protective caps from the iFA+ and iFN+ bottles.
Wipe the septum with a sterile alcohol wipe.
Vortex the test article to ensure a homogenous suspension.
Inoculate the bottles with the validated volume of the test article using a sterile syringe and hypodermic needle.
Wipe the septum with a sterile alcohol wipe after inoculation.
Incubate the bottles on the BacT/ALERT Dual-T instrument as described in Table 1.
Inoculate the SAB plate with the validated amount of the test article using a pipettor.
Streak for isolation using a sterile loop.
Let stand for 10 min to ensure the sample does not run onto the plate lid when inverted for incubation.
Place each SAB plate inoculated with the test article into a plastic bag.
Tie loosely and incubate as described in Table 1.
Aseptically close the TSA and SAB settling plates.
Document the sampling end time.
Perform GFS as described in step 3.2.
Wipe gloves with 70% sIPA after sampling.
Loosely bag the plates.
Incubate cultures as described in Table 1.
Visually inspect BacT/ALERT bottles at the end of incubation period.
Transfer all test materials out of the BSC.
Clean the BSC as per step 1.4.
